integrity: The infinite classification is proved from an exact private-neighbor criterion for every selected vertex. Counting and maximality are then derived from the complete case split. The accompanying exhaustive program independently checks every vertex subset of \(\operatorname{Cr}_n\) for \(3\le n\le8\), but that finite computation is used only as verification, not as an infinite proof.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is restricted to ordinary closed-neighborhood irredundance in crown graphs. It does not claim analogous formulas for open, total, edge-vertex, vertex-edge, or side-restricted irredundance variants. Exhaustive computation covers only \(3\le n\le8\); the all-\(n\) theorem is supported by the structural private-neighbor proof. An older equivalent formulation under a less common graph name remains a bibliographic risk.
title: Irredundant and maximal irredundant sets of crown graphs
